رَحِيمُ : see الرَّحْمٰنُ, in seven places. ―
-b2- Sometimes it is syn. with ↓ مَرْحُومٌ [i. e. Treated, or regarded, with mercy or pity or compassion; &c.: see 1, first sentence]: 'Amelles Ibn-'Akeel says, (using it in this sense, Ham p. 628,) “فَأَمَّا إِذَا عَضَّتْ بِكَ الحَرْبُ عَضَّةً
فَإِنَّكَ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلَيْكَ رَحِيمُ
” (S, and Ham,) i. e. [But at all events,] when war becomes [once] severe to thee, and thine enemy has almost overcome thee, [verily thou art regarded with favour,] treated with mercy, and defended, by us. (Ham.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
